name: Mercury
mythology: Named after the Roman messenger god Mercury (Greek: Hermes), known for his speed. The fastest planet seemed a fitting tribute to the swift-footed deity who delivered messages between gods and mortals.
fun_facts: Smallest planet, closest to the Sun. Has the most eccentric orbit of all planets. One day on Mercury (sunrise to sunrise) lasts 176 Earth days! Surface temperature varies from -290°F to 800°F. Has a large iron core making it very dense. No atmosphere to speak of.

name: Venus
mythology: Named after the Roman goddess of love and beauty (Greek: Aphrodite). As the brightest natural object in the night sky after the Moon, ancient observers found it beautiful and worthy of the goddess's name.
fun_facts: Hottest planet in our solar system at 900°F due to runaway greenhouse effect. Rotates backwards (retrograde) compared to most planets. A day on Venus (243 Earth days) is longer than its year (225 Earth days)! Thick clouds of sulfuric acid. Atmospheric pressure is 90x Earth's. Called Earth's 'sister planet' due to similar size.

name: Mars
mythology: Named after the Roman god of war (Greek: Ares) due to its blood-red color, which ancient cultures associated with bloodshed and battle. The planet's two moons, Phobos (Fear) and Deimos (Dread), are named after the god's companions.
fun_facts: The Red Planet gets its color from iron oxide (rust). Home to Olympus Mons, the largest volcano in the solar system (3x height of Mt. Everest). Has polar ice caps of water and CO2. Day length is very similar to Earth (24.6 hours). Dust storms can engulf the entire planet. Future target for human colonization.

name: Jupiter
mythology: Named after the king of the Roman gods (Greek: Zeus), ruler of the sky and thunder. As the largest planet, it deserved the name of the most powerful deity. Its moons are named after Zeus's lovers and descendants.
fun_facts: Largest planet - could fit all other planets inside it. The Great Red Spot is a storm larger than Earth that has raged for at least 400 years. Has faint rings. Strongest magnetic field of any planet. Rotates fastest - a day is less than 10 hours. Acts as a 'cosmic vacuum cleaner' protecting inner planets from asteroids. Has 95 known moons including the four large Galilean moons.

name: Saturn
mythology: Named after the Roman god of agriculture and time (Greek: Cronus), father of Jupiter. In mythology, Saturn was dethroned by Jupiter, just as the planet Saturn is 'second' to Jupiter in size and brightness.
fun_facts: Famous for its spectacular ring system made of ice and rock particles. Rings are 175,000 miles wide but only 30 feet thick! Least dense planet - would float in water. Has hexagonal storm at north pole. Titan, its largest moon, has lakes of liquid methane and is larger than Mercury. Has 146 known moons, most in the solar system.

name: Uranus
mythology: Named after the Greek god of the sky, Uranus (father of Saturn/Cronus). The only planet named after a Greek rather than Roman deity. Discovered in 1781 by William Herschel, breaking the tradition of planets known since antiquity.
fun_facts: Rotates on its side - axial tilt of 98°, possibly due to ancient collision. This means it has the most extreme seasons in the solar system. Appears blue-green due to methane in atmosphere. Very cold at -320°F. Has faint rings discovered in 1977. Winds can reach 560 mph. Has 27 known moons named after Shakespeare and Pope characters.

name: Neptune
mythology: Named after the Roman god of the sea (Greek: Poseidon), fitting for its deep blue color resembling ocean waters. Discovered in 1846 through mathematical predictions rather than observation - a triumph of celestial mechanics.
fun_facts: Windiest planet with speeds up to 1,200 mph. Deep blue color from methane in atmosphere. Has the Great Dark Spot, similar to Jupiter's Great Red Spot but it comes and goes. Coldest planet atmosphere at -330°F. Has faint rings. Its moon Triton orbits backwards and may be a captured Kuiper Belt object. Triton has geysers of nitrogen gas.

name: Pluto
mythology: Named after the Roman god of the underworld (Greek: Hades) in 1930 by 11-year-old Venetia Burney. The name fit a distant, cold world in the outer darkness of the solar system. Reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006, sparking public outcry.
fun_facts: Heart-shaped region called Tombaugh Regio discovered by New Horizons in 2015. Has a tenuous atmosphere that freezes and falls as snow when farther from the Sun. Its largest moon Charon is so big (half Pluto's size) they orbit a common point in space between them. Surface has mountains made of water ice as hard as rock. Nitrogen glaciers flow across the surface. Takes 248 years to orbit the Sun. Sometimes closer to Sun than Neptune.
